channel.title: Latest alerts from washingtonpost.com
channel.description: An unofficial feed created by Derek Willis.

item.title: Michigan elects Abdul El-Sayed as nation’s first Muslim senator, AP reports, giving Democrats at least 54 votes in chamber
item.description: El-Sayed defeated former congressman Mike Rogers (R) in one of the most closely watched and hard-fought contests of the midterms. He will succeed Sen. Gary Peters (D), who is retiring.

item.title: Democrats take control of House and Senate as voters deal Trump a historic repudiation in midterms
item.description: Democrats won in places they hadn’t carried in decades amid voter discontent over high prices and the war in Iran. Republicans also suffered from a collapse in turnout, as fewer of their supporters showed up on Election Day than four years ago, according to preliminary turnout data.

item.title: Sen. Susan Collins (R) of Maine loses reelection bid to Troy Jackson (D), according to AP
item.description: Collins, who was seeking a sixth term, had distanced herself from President Donald Trump while campaigning in the blue state. Jackson, the former president of the state Senate, became Democrats’ pick after Graham Platner withdrew.

item.title: How Trump and Democrats can navigate divided government
item.description: How Trump and Democrats can navigate divided government

item.title: Democrats made the midterms about Trump. Voters responded, David Ignatius writes.
item.description: Democrats made the midterms about Trump. Voters responded, David Ignatius writes.

item.title: Democrats win control of Senate, as Josh Turek flips seat in Iowa, according to AP
item.description: Democrats have now seized GOP seats in Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, North Carolina, South Carolina and Texas, giving them the majority in the Senate. Turek, a member of the state legislature, targeted President Donald Trump’s tariffs and high gas prices driven by the Iran war. He will succeed Sen. Joni Ernst (R), who is retiring.

item.title: Kansas picks a Democrat for Senate for the first time in nearly a century, ousting incumbent Roger Marshall (R), AP reports
item.description: The first-term senator lost to Adam Hamilton (D), the founding pastor of a megachurch who received endorsements from some of the state’s former Republican governors.

item.title: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott (R) loses his bid for a fourth term, falling to Gina Hinojosa (D), according to AP
item.description: Hinojosa, who serves in the state legislature, will be Texas’s first Democratic governor in more than 30 years.

item.title: Sherrod Brown (D) wins Senate race in Ohio, toppling incumbent Jon Husted (R), according to AP
item.description: Ohio was one of Democrats’ prime targets for flipping a GOP Senate seat. Brown previously spent 18 years in the chamber before losing in 2024 as the state turned increasingly Republican.

item.title: James Talarico (D) wins Senate race in Texas, seizing Republican-held seat, according to AP
item.description: Talarico defeated Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton (R) in the traditionally red state, in one of the most closely watched races of the midterms. He will succeed Sen. John Cornyn (R), who lost in the primary.

item.title: Amy Acton (D) tops Vivek Ramaswamy (R) in race for Ohio governor, according to AP
item.description: The victory by Acton, who helped to direct Ohio’s early response to the covid-19 pandemic, suggested the state could be shifting toward the middle again after becoming deeply red over the past decade.

item.title: Sen. Darline Graham (R) is defeated in South Carolina, AP reports, a major breakthrough in Democrats’ efforts to flip the chamber
item.description: Graham lost in an upset to Annie Andrews (D). Graham was seeking a full term after being appointed in July to fill the seat of her brother, the late Sen. Lindsey Graham.

item.title: Janeese Lewis George (D) declares victory in D.C. mayoral race, marking a political shift to the left in the nation’s capital
item.description: Lewis George, a democratic socialist, faced nominal opposition in the deep-blue District of Columbia, where the Democratic primary is the most consequential contest.

item.title: Rep. Tom Kean Jr. (R) of N.J. loses reelection, according to AP. His four-month House absence fueled intrigue and GOP concern.
item.description: Kean lost to Navy veteran Rebecca Bennett (D) in one of the nation’s most vulnerable Republican districts. Kean’s prolonged absence drew national media attention and went unexplained until he disclosed in June that he had received treatment for depression.

item.title: Georgia elects its first Black governor, AP reports. Keisha Lance Bottoms is the first Democrat to win the role in nearly 30 years.
item.description: Bottoms, a former Atlanta mayor, triumphed despite the financial edge held by Republican Rick Jackson.

item.title: Virginia voters approve constitutional amendment enshrining the right to an abortion with some restrictions, according to AP
item.description: The amendment restricts abortion during the third trimester unless “the patient’s health is at risk or the pregnancy cannot survive.”

item.title: Democrats flip first House district with Jamie Ager’s win in North Carolina as the party hopes to seize control from Republicans
item.description: Democrats need to net only three House seats to win the majority. Republicans currently have 219 seats, including one held by an independent who caucuses with them, to Democrats’ 214, with two vacancies.

item.title: Roy Cooper (D) wins Senate race in North Carolina, AP reports. The former governor flipped a GOP seat.
item.description: Cooper defeated Michael Whatley (R), a former chair of the Republican National Committee. Cooper will succeed Sen. Thom Tillis (R), who is retiring.

item.title: Blue wave or red riptide? See how counties are shifting in the 2026 Senate and House midterms.
item.description: Track in real time where voters across the country are backing Democrats or Republicans compared to their support in 2024.

item.title: ‘Signs of real Republican erosion’: 9 writers discuss the midterms
item.description: Columnists and writers James Hohmann, Megan McArdle, Ramesh Ponnuru, Jim Geraghty, Dominic Pino, Kate Andrews, Carine Hajjar, Theodore R. Johnson and James Desio will offer real-time commentary on what to watch, exit polls, voter turnout and more on Election Day.

item.title: Gov. Wes Moore (D) wins Maryland governor’s race, according to AP, defeating Republican Dan Cox in a rematch of their 2022 contest
item.description: Moore has deflected questions about a presidential bid but has acknowledged he wants to be “part of the conversation” in 2028. He recently rallied Black and veteran voters in Virginia, which will be an early Democratic presidential primary state.

item.title: Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff of Georgia is reelected, according to AP. His victory is key to Democrats’ plan to win the Senate.
item.description: Ossoff defeated GOP Rep. Mike Collins. Ossoff was the only Democratic Senate incumbent defending a seat in a state that President Donald Trump won in 2024.

item.title: Trump touted his Reflecting Pool success. But new problems are visible.
item.description: Discoloration and inconsistencies were spotted immediately following the president’s speech.

item.title: Control of Congress is at stake in this election. Follow our live updates and the results of key Senate, House and governor races.
item.description: The first polls have closed in Indiana and Kentucky. The open race to replace Rep. Andy Barr (R-Kentucky) could give the earliest indication of how the night is going for each party.

item.title: Google researchers are fighting the company to tell the world what they know about AI
item.description: Employment contracts deter staff from warning the public about AI risks, current workers said.

item.title: ‘Rightly furious’: Five writers reveal why they’re voting in this election
item.description: What is bringing Post Opinions writers to the ballot box?

item.title: More people are having strokes before 55. Here’s what experts know.
item.description: High blood pressure and diabetes may partly explain the rise documented in a new study. Reducing your risk starts long before symptoms appear.

item.title: The unlikely player in contentious Michigan Senate race: Haley Stevens’s fiancé
item.description: Jason Turkish took on a role in Stevens’s campaign that rankled staff, according to multiple people who worked for her.

item.title: Will Trump or others interfere with voting? What to know about election security.
item.description: President Donald Trump has taken unprecedented steps to insert himself and the government into Election Day, but election officials are projecting calm.

item.title: Election Day voting is underway. Here are the key early races to watch and what their outcomes might suggest.
item.description: Races in Kentucky, Virginia and Florida may provide early answers on whether a Democratic wave many expect will materialize.

item.title: Frailty in older adults is not inevitable. Here’s how to reverse it.
item.description: A new study shows the benefits of vigorous walking for older adults.

item.title: Supreme Court denies Trump administration request to set aside more than 20,000 California ballots
item.description: The ruling is the latest setback for the Justice Department, which has waged an aggressive legal campaign to influence how states run elections.

item.title: Inside Elon Musk’s plan to upend the wireless phone industry
item.description: SpaceX is in talks to buy Boost Mobile or use its network, giving Musk a potential back door into the $235 billion wireless market.

item.title: A terrible night awaits the GOP, and even that might be an understatement
item.description: Henry Olsen’s final midterm prediction is a Democratic House and Senate.

item.title: Trump administration lays out plan to overhaul D.C. golf course, but proposal lacks details on cost and timing
item.description: The Washington Post obtained the 55-page proposal, which calls for a new championship golf course and a seawall around Hains Point. The National Capital Planning Commission is scheduled to consider the concept proposal at its Dec. 3 meeting, more than two weeks after Nov. 15, the date administration officials have said they intend to close East Potomac Golf Links.

item.title: Binance says it has covered 95% of crypto assets taken in record $6.3 billion hack
item.description: Cryptocurrency exchanges have been a frequent target of hacks by North Koreans and have not always been able to repay users afterward.

item.title: Trump touts Reflecting Pool renovations as he makes midterm closing arguments
item.description: The president spoke Monday at the historic pool in front of the Lincoln Memorial, about six months after he began rushed renovations that quickly went awry. The longtime real estate developer has insisted the project shows how he can fix Washington — and one of its signature monuments.

item.title: Paul Anka, Andy Garcia, Barbara Mandrell are among those who will receive Kennedy Center Honors at first off-site awards ceremony
item.description: Singers Paul Anka and Barbara Mandrell, music producer David Foster, actor Andy Garcia and playwright David Mamet will be celebrated Dec. 7 at Capital One Arena.

item.title: Carolyn Hax: My wealthier siblings decided on our mom’s care plan without me
item.description: Adapted from the “Life Hax” podcast: A letter writer is angry their siblings chose such an expensive facility for Mom.

item.title: Trump administration asks Supreme Court to set aside 20,000 California ballots for now
item.description: The appeal came in a fast-moving legal dispute over midterm ballots that the Trump administration claims may have been cast by noncitizens in the state.

item.title: Charges against FBI agents in Hunter Biden laptop investigation are dismissed
item.description: A federal magistrate judge said the Justice Department had failed to show probable cause that two former FBI officials made false statements to the House Judiciary Committee as it investigated President Joe Biden’s son in the lead-up to the 2024 presidential election.

item.title: The GOP’s midterms meltdown has one author, Charles Lane writes
item.description: President Trump singlehandedly turned a winnable election into a Democratic rout.

item.title: Milton Coleman, a barrier-breaking editor at The Post, dies at 79
item.description: The former deputy managing editor was the first African American journalist on The Post’s masthead. He mentored generations of younger journalists and championed diversity across the news industry.

item.description: As Vance campaigns for Republicans facing midterm headwinds, he is also building a political brand beyond President Donald Trump.

item.title: Inside the chaos before Haley Stevens’s shocking Senate endorsement in Michigan
item.description: The decision by Rep. Haley Stevens to endorse Republican Mike Rogers in the Senate race is deeply personal – and highlights Democrats' fractures over Israel policy.

item.title: Crash of business jet in Florida neighborhood kills all 9 on board, transportation secretary says
item.description: The aircraft was en route from Texas to the Bahamas when it crashed in West Palm Beach. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy called it a “horrific tragedy.”

item.title: Here’s what to do every day to boost your immune system
item.description: Taking these steps can help your body fight off germs that cause ailments like the common cold.
